s2-ship-town-v1.prompt: A small coastal town seen from the deck of a ship offshore across calm water. Along a curving pebble shore stand about forty small cottages, and every cottage roof is a whole wooden rowing boat or fishing boat turned upside down: a rounded hull with the keel running along the top and the planks curving down to the walls, no pitched roofs anywhere. In the middle of the town a long hall is roofed with an entire large cargo ship turned keel-up, its smooth planked hull curving down to the stone walls, bow at one end and stern at the other. A wooden quay, two masts in the harbour, low hills behind. A ship's rail cuts across the near foreground. Pen and ink field sketch in a travel sketchbook: confident sepia-black ink linework on cream paper, shading done only with hatching and cross-hatching, almost no colour, at most a faint grey wash in the shadows, loose unfinished edges fading into blank paper, visible paper texture. No text, no lettering, no handwriting, no numbers, no signature.
